checklist.notes: The core tense and narrative examples are suitable for A2.2, but the unsupported task wording includes ‘ongoing movement’, ‘explicitly agrees’, ‘the contrast determines’, and ‘prominence matches one stated contrast’.
The retell converts An’s future commitment ‘I’ll carry’ into the completed event ‘An carried’ although the source dialogue never states that the action happened.
Individual sentences and the help exchange are grammatical and understandable; the principal defect is unsupported event meaning rather than surface idiomaticity.
The repeated movement-sense definition is expected target reuse within the supplied lessons; no suspicious unexplained internal copying or external check occurred.
The lesson reviews authorized past continuous, request-for-help, sentence stress, movement run, and narrative sequence using only prior past and pronunciation concepts.
All text is English and embedded concept/vocabulary identifiers remain within the exact regenerated scope.

methods: Manual comparison of lesson wording with the supplied authoritative request and project-authored teaching payload.
Exact contiguous-word overlap comparison across the ten supplied v3 lesson bodies.
Inspection of the accepted audit provenance/copyright scope without consulting external sources.
copyright_originality_check.scope_limitations: No suspicious unexplained copying was found within the supplied scope. Reuse of target forms, short pedagogical frames, and project-authored definitions/examples is expected. No external search was performed; this is not a plagiarism clearance or copyright guarantee.

findings.description: Section 2 establishes only a promise (‘I’ll carry the books’), but Section 3 presents ‘Finally, An carried the books’ as a completed fact. A retell should not change an intended future action into an event known to have happened.
findings.recommendation: Either add source text showing that An subsequently carried the books, or retell the fourth step as ‘Finally, An agreed to carry the books.’

findings.description: The final two sections express the speaking and self-check tasks through dense abstract language above A2.2, without scaffolding for terms such as ‘prominence’, ‘stated contrast’, and ‘ongoing movement’.
findings.recommendation: Use short numbered prompts and concrete stress marks, with a simple explanation or Vietnamese gloss for prominence.

limitations: Review used only the exact lesson, accepted audit, regenerated hash-matching authoritative request, and verified M5 development snapshot; generator reasoning and prior review records were excluded.
No audio was supplied; pronunciation judgments cover written instructions and IPA only, not realized speech or learner performance.
No external CEFR vocabulary profiler or corpus was used; CEFR findings are qualitative independent AI judgments about the learner-facing text.

Originality checking was limited to the supplied authoritative payload and the ten supplied v3 lessons; no Internet, external corpus, or plagiarism search was performed, so no external plagiarism or legal-clearance claim is made.
